title: Your Spring Revenue Is Climbing. Your Margin Might Be Sliding Underneath It.
linkedin:
Revenue is climbing for a lot of East Coast businesses right now. Spring trading is doing what spring trading does.

Here's the part worth sitting with: a rising revenue line and a rising profit line are not the same thing, and this time of year is exactly when they tend to quietly separate.

We see it most often in the mix. A business fills its diary again after a quieter winter, and the work that comes in first is usually the work that was easiest to win, which is often the work priced the lowest. Add a run of overtime or casual hours to meet the demand, and the cost base shifts in a way the monthly P&L doesn't flag on its own.

Nobody did anything wrong. The business simply grew in a direction that happened to carry less margin, and the top line alone can't tell you which direction that was.

The fix isn't complicated. Rank each product or service line by what it actually contributes once its own costs are counted, not the business average. It's usually not the busiest line that comes out on top.

A rising revenue number is worth celebrating. Knowing exactly where the margin sits underneath it is worth a great deal more.

Full piece on the ProfitPulse blog.
